related.title: EU accused of dragging its feet over ban on trade with illegal Israeli settlements
related.summary: EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels on Monday will discuss a possible ban on imports from the settlements, against an ongoing humanitarian crisis in Gaza, where a UN inquiry found Israel to be committing a genocide, and surging state-backed violence in the occupied West Bank, which has killed at least 235 children. Under the EU-Israel agreement, goods from the occupied Palestinian territories (the Golan Heights, Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem) are not entitled to the preferential trade terms that apply to Israel.
bullets: EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels on Monday will discuss a possible ban on imports from the settlements, against an ongoing humanitarian crisis in Gaza, where a UN inquiry found Israel to be committing a genocide, and surging state-backed violence in the occupied West Bank, which has killed at least 235 children.

Under the EU-Israel agreement, goods from the occupied Palestinian territories (the Golan Heights, Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem) are not entitled to the preferential trade terms that apply to Israel.

At least 10 European member states, including Belgium, the Netherlands and Spain, say the EU has an obligation to end trade with occupied territories, following a ruling from the international court of justice (ICJ) in 2024 that called on Israel to end its occupation of the Palestinian territories “as rapidly as possible”.
It said that states had to “take steps to prevent trade or investment relations that assists in the maintenance of the illegal situation created by Israel in the occupied Palestinian territory”.

Ignacio García Bercero, a former senior trade official at the commission, who signed the letter, said: “The only way to ensure compliance with the opinion of the ICJ is a ban on trade with the illegal settlements.
related.excerpt: The EU has been accused of dragging its feet over upholding international law, on the eve of a long-awaited debate about banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements. EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels on Monday will discuss a possible ban on imports from the settlements, against an ongoing humanitarian crisis in Gaza, where a UN inquiry found Israel to be committing a genocide, and surging state-backed violence in the occupied West Bank, which has killed at least 235 children. But the 27 ministers are not expected to take decisions about trade amid persistent divisions about how to respond to Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and his government. A part or total ban on imports from settlements is one of three options presented by the European Commission in a paper seen by the Guardian. The other two options are high tariffs that make trade economically unviable or an import licensing system. The leaked paper was first reported by Euronews. bullets: LATIN AMERICA & THE CARIBBEAN Weekly Situation Update As of 10 July 2026 The boundaries and names shown and the designations used on this map do not imply official endorsement or acceptance by the United Nations.

Following visits to affected communities and meetings with national and international humanitarian partners, UN Under- Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher announced an appeal for an additional US$298 million to meet the needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.

The population requiring humanitarian food assistance across the country is expected to rise gradually to between 4.0 and 4.99 million people, with poor rural, Indigenous, Afro-Colombian, Venezuelan migrant, and informal urban households identified as populations of highest concern.
In Kenscoff, attacks beginning the night of 4-5 July and spreading on 8 July displaced 5,840 people (1,836 households).
According to FEWS NET’s latest outlook, crisis (IPC Phase 3) levels of food insecurity are expected to persist through January 2027 in the departments of La Guajira and Chocó.
